title: Unable to disable text formatting unless the cursor is against a non-whitespace character or highlighted text
line: Sticky Note's Bold, Italic, Underline and Strikethrough buttons now switch formatting on or off for what you type next, even after a space or in an empty note.
explanation: Sticky Note's DocumentHandler formats text through its own QTextCursor, not the TextArea's, so without a selection it could only merge the format into the word under the cursor. After a space or in an empty note there was no word, so the button did nothing and stayed in its old state; next to a word it reformatted the already-typed word. Now, without a selection, the chosen format is kept as pending for the cursor position, shown in the button state, and merged into the text typed there (in the same undo step); moving the cursor drops it.

commits.message:
applets/notes: Apply formatting to the next typed text without a selection

Without a selection, the formatting buttons changed the word under the
cursor and could not be turned off after a space or in an empty note. Now
they set the format for the text typed next, and only change a selection.

BUG: 526478

media.caption: Master: typed 'word', clicked Bold (the existing word turns bold), typed a space and clicked Bold again to turn it off: the button stays on and 'plain' comes out bold.
Fixed: typed 'word ', clicked Bold (button on, 'word' untouched), typed 'bold', clicked Bold off, typed ' plain': only 'bold' is bold.

review.text: The UX direction matches the reporter's request and standard rich-text editors by applying formatting without a selection to newly typed text instead of reformatting the existing word. However, tracking pending formatting via a raw character-count delta in setCursorPosition() has several state-management bugs: both m_pendingPosition and m_cursorPosition initialize to -1, pending state is not cleared in setTarget() or when a selection is created without moving the cursor, forward-Delete breaks the character-count delta so the next typed character loses its pending format, and an undo that inserts text at m_pendingPosition can trigger joinPreviousEditBlock() and corrupt the undo stack. Tightening the pending-state lifecycle will make this ready to merge.
changes: Guard currentCharFormat() with m_pendingPosition >= 0 (since both m_pendingPosition and m_cursorPosition initialize to -1) and bail out of mergeFormatOnSelectionOrNextText() if m_cursorPosition < 0 or !m_doc.

Reset m_pendingFormat, m_pendingPosition = -1, and m_pendingCharacterCount = 0 in setTarget(), and clear pending formatting whenever a non-empty selection is set in setSelectionStart()/setSelectionEnd().

Replace or harden the characterCount() delta heuristic (e.g. connect to QTextDocument::contentsChange to clear pending state on removals/non-adjacent edits and avoid applying pending format during undo) so forward-Delete at m_pendingPosition does not silently drop pending formatting and Ctrl+Z cannot trigger joinPreviousEditBlock().

reviews.text: Fixes exactly what the reporter described: format buttons now toggle the format for the next typed text after a space or in an empty note, and only touch existing text when it is selected; the after screenshot and the regression notes (undo grouping, selection, cursor move dropping the pending format) back it up. The pending-format tracker in DocumentHandler is the pragmatic route, since QtQuick exposes no way to set the TextArea's own insertion format (even TextEdit.cursorSelection falls back to WordUnderCursor on a copy of the cursor). The one debatable point is dropping word-under-cursor formatting when the caret is inside a word (word processors keep it), but the reporter asked for that, and the notes and commit message say so plainly.
